1) Conditional purge triggers – our clause asks for an automatic scheduled purge (30d after TTL) but Carried Forward exceptions / legal holds could extend that. We need a clear description of how and when a scheduled purge is skipped, and what evidence you provide that the skip happened because of an active hold.

3) Erase certification — our audit requires a machine-readable proof-of-erasure for a record-level delete (not just a log entry). Do you provide per-request delete certificates or a periodic evidence package (e.g., weekly/monthly) for deletes in scope?

Nikhil / team — summary from infra/ops perspective below. Keeping it intentionally short so Legal can map to contract terms: 

1) Conditional purge / legal hold
- Operationally, a record delete goes through two phases: tombstone (logical delete) and eventual expunge (physical deletion from primary storage).
- Scheduled purges operate on the expunge phase: automated job picks objects with expired TTL and not flagged by an active hold. Holds are implemented as metadata flags in the metadata DB and are globally checked by the expunge job at the time of run.
- Evidence we produce when a purge is skipped: expunge job logs (job id, timestamp, object ids skipped, hold id). We also emit an internal event (hold.applied) that links the hold id to the TTL extension.

2) Onshore backups and snapshots
- Backups are daily snapshots kept for 30 days by default. Snapshots are geo-redundant but we can offer an "onshore snapshot" option for an account-level commitment (adds a small premium).
- Snapshot restoration paths: snapshots are immutable; to fully remove data we run a scheduled background job that purges from snapshot index metadata then rotates cold storage segments. That process can take up to 14 days to guarantee removal from long-term snapshot storage in the worst-case (delays due to compaction and cold-region retention).

3) Erase certification / evidence format
- We provide per-request delete certificates (JSON) for API-initiated erasures when requested as part of the delete call. The certificate contains: object id set, expunge job id, expunge timestamp (RFC3339), and a signed hash (HMAC) referencing the job output.
- For bulk/DDL deletes or scheduled purges we provide a batched attestations package (JSON Lines) weekly that maps to job ids and object id ranges.

Implications / recommended DPA language points for Legal: 
- Define 'retain until' (TTL) and 'active legal hold' and tie the expunge job behavior to those terms.
- Specify snapshot window: "Backups and snapshots may persist for up to 14 days beyond primary expunge unless an onshore-only backup option is selected."
- Specify evidence options: per-request JSON certificate on-demand OR weekly batch JSONL attestations.

I'll attach a short proposed paragraph for the DPA. Marcus

[Attachment: Redwood_Delete_Playbook_v1.pdf]

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear asks and for the redline. Below is a concise operational summary you can attach to the DPA; I’ve highlighted the options you can choose in the contract and the evidence deliverables we can commit to.

Operational summary (for inclusion in the DPA):
- Delete flow: Redwood performs a two-phase delete: a logical tombstone is applied immediately and records are scheduled for physical expunge once the configured TTL expires and no active legal hold applies.
- Legal holds: Holds are represented as system-level flags. If a hold applies to a record at expunge time the object is skipped. Redwood will produce expunge job logs that reference the hold id and object ids skipped; these logs are retained per the Audit Log retention schedule and can be shared with customers under an NDA.
- Backups / snapshots: Primary data is snapshotted daily and snapshots are geo-redundant by default. If you require an onshore-only backup option, Redwood can enable account-level onshore snapshots (subject to a premium). In the event of an expunge, snapshot metadata is reconciled and cold-storage segments are rotated; full removal from snapshot-backed cold storage can take up to 14 days in edge cases.
- Erase evidence: Customers may choose one of two evidence modes: (1) Per-request JSON delete certificates (issued on demand at the time of an API-initiated expunge); or (2) Weekly batched attestations in JSON Lines format listing job ids and object id ranges for scheduled purges. Certificates include expunge job id, RFC3339 timestamp, and an HMAC-signed job digest for integrity.

Proposed DPA clauses we suggest adding: 
- "Redwood will provide, upon request, a machine-readable expunge certificate (JSON) for any customer-initiated record-level delete. For scheduled purges, Redwood will deliver weekly batched attestations; customers may also request ad-hoc per-request certificates for scheduled jobs at mutual cost."
- "Snapshots and backups may persist up to 14 days beyond primary expunge to allow for snapshot compaction; an onshore-only snapshot configuration is available via account-level commitment."
- "If a legal hold prevents expunge of records, Redwood will supply expunge-job logs referencing skipped object ids and the related hold id for audit."

Attachments: I’ve attached our internal delete playbook (Redwood_Delete_Playbook_v1.pdf) which explains the expunge job lifecycle and sample JSON schema for the erase certificate. I’ve also attached a short draft of proposed DPA wording for you to insert into your redline (proposed-dpa-language-tnc.txt).

If this aligns with Aurum’s needs let me know and we can incorporate the exact option you want (per-request certs vs weekly attestations) into the DPA redline. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if Legal prefers.
